questions.stem:
Statement: 'Carry an umbrella whenever you go out.' Which assumption is implicit?
I. It may rain when one goes out.
II. People generally do not carry umbrellas.

options.option_text: Only I is implicit (correct: the advice 'carry umbrella' assumes possible rain is a reason to do so; II is not necessarily assumed — the advice doesn't depend on what people generally do ✓)
Only II is implicit (II is not the basis for this advice)
Both I and II are implicit (II is not required to justify the statement)
Neither is implicit (I is clearly the underlying assumption)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I (may rain when one goes out) is implicit — this is precisely why the advice to carry an umbrella makes sense. Without this assumption, the advice has no basis. Assumption II (people don't carry umbrellas) is NOT implicit — the advice doesn't depend on what others do; it's general advice.

questions.stem: Statement: 'If you want to be fit, exercise daily.' Which assumption is implicit?

options.option_text: Everyone wants to be fit (NOT implicit — the statement only gives advice to those who want fitness, not assuming everyone does)
Daily exercise contributes to fitness (correct: this is the underlying assumption — without it, the advice has no logical basis ✓)
Exercise is difficult for most people (not mentioned; difficulty is not assumed)
Only daily exercise can make one fit (too strong; the statement says 'if you want to be fit, exercise daily' — not that this is the only way)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The implicit assumption is that daily exercise helps achieve fitness — otherwise, the advice would be pointless. 'Everyone wants fitness' is not assumed (the conditional 'if you want' acknowledges not everyone does). 'Only way' is too absolute — the statement doesn't say exercise is the ONLY path to fitness.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The government has decided to increase the minimum wage.' Which assumption is implicit?
I. Workers were earning below a sustainable wage.
II. An increase in minimum wage will benefit workers.

options.option_text: Only I (I: workers earning below sustainable wage — this may explain motivation but isn't NECESSARILY the assumption; II is more directly implied)
Only II (correct: the government's decision assumes that increasing the wage will benefit workers — otherwise, why increase it? I is a possible background, not necessarily an explicit assumption ✓)
Both I and II (I is possible context but not definitely an assumption)
Neither (II is clearly implicit — the decision implies expected benefit)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The government raising minimum wages IMPLICITLY assumes this will benefit workers (II) — otherwise the decision makes no sense. Assumption I (workers earning below sustainable wage) is a background condition that might motivate the policy but is not what's assumed in the decision itself — it could be stated or may not apply to all workers.

questions.stem: Statement: 'Read the instructions carefully before starting the examination.' What is implicit?

options.option_text: Instructions are difficult to understand (wrong — difficulty is not assumed; careful reading is for any instructions)

Candidates sometimes make mistakes due to not reading instructions (correct: if everyone always read instructions carefully, the reminder would be unnecessary; the assumption is that not reading instructions causes problems ✓)
The examination is very important (exam importance isn't what makes this instruction necessary)
Instructions are written in a foreign language (not at all assumed)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The instruction to 'read carefully' implies that (1) not reading carefully leads to mistakes, and (2) candidates might not read them otherwise. If mistakes from skipping instructions weren't a real risk, the reminder would be pointless. This is the implicit assumption.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Bank XYZ: For all your financial needs.' Which assumptions are implicit?
I. Bank XYZ offers a wide range of financial services.
II. People need financial assistance.

options.option_text: Only I (correct: 'for all your financial needs' assumes the bank offers diverse services (I). II is a very general fact not specifically assumed by this ad — people broadly need financial services is a general fact, not an assumption this specific statement rests on)
Only II (II is a general fact, not a specific assumption of this statement)
Both I and II (II is too general to be an implicit assumption here)
Neither (I clearly follows from 'all your financial needs')

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'For all your financial needs' implicitly assumes that Bank XYZ can fulfill all such needs (I) — otherwise the claim is false. Assumption II (people need financial assistance) is a general fact, not specific to this statement. In S&A questions, distinguish between assumptions specific to the statement vs general known facts.

questions.stem: Statement: 'The patient should not eat solid food for 24 hours after the surgery.' What is the implicit assumption?

options.option_text: Surgery is a dangerous procedure (surgery risk is general knowledge; not the specific assumption behind this instruction)
Eating solid food too soon after surgery may cause complications (correct: this is exactly what the instruction protects against — the assumption is that early solid food is harmful ✓)
The patient cannot eat after surgery anyway (wrong: the instruction implies the patient CAN eat but SHOULD NOT)
All patients recover at the same rate (not assumed; the 24-hour window is a standard precaution)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The instruction 'no solid food for 24 hours' assumes that eating solid food too soon could cause harm (complications such as nausea, disrupted healing, risk of aspiration, etc.). This is the medical rationale underlying the instruction — it's the implicit assumption.

questions.stem: Statement: 'Students who score above 90% in the entrance exam will be given a scholarship.' Which assumption is implicit?

options.option_text: All students want a scholarship (not necessarily; students who don't apply don't need this assumption)
Some students will score above 90% in the entrance exam (correct: the statement only makes sense if the scholarship is actually achievable — i.e., some students can score above 90% ✓)
Students below 90% do not deserve financial help (the statement doesn't suggest other students are undeserving)
The entrance exam is very difficult (difficulty isn't assumed; the threshold might be hard or easy)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The scholarship policy assumes that at least some students CAN score above 90% — otherwise the policy is meaningless (a scholarship for an impossible criterion). This is a fundamental implicit assumption: the criterion is achievable.

questions.stem: Statement: 'Always keep a first-aid kit at home.' Which assumption is NOT implicit?

options.option_text: Minor injuries or emergencies can occur at home (implicit — this is why you'd need a first-aid kit)
A first-aid kit can help manage minor injuries (implicit — the recommendation assumes first-aid kits are useful)
People should not go to hospitals (NOT implicit: the statement is about home first-aid, not about avoiding hospitals ✓)
People often overlook keeping first-aid kits (possibly implicit — the advice is given because people need reminding)

questions.explanation: C is correct. The statement 'keep a first-aid kit at home' does NOT imply avoiding hospitals. It's simply a preparedness measure for immediate response to minor injuries. The recommendation to use first aid doesn't contradict or replace hospital visits — the assumption that 'people should not go to hospitals' is NEVER implied.

questions.stem: Statement: 'The train may be delayed due to fog.' Which assumption is implicit?

options.option_text: Trains always run on time normally (implied: the unusual nature of the delay suggests normally trains run on schedule)
Fog reduces visibility and can disrupt train operations (correct: the link between fog and train delay assumes that fog affects train visibility/signalling ✓)
It will definitely be foggy (wrong: 'may be' indicates uncertainty — not a definite assumption)
Passengers should take a different mode of transport (the statement doesn't suggest alternatives)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Saying fog causes train delay implies that fog disrupts train visibility and operations (signalling systems, driving speed). This causal link is the implicit assumption. 'Definitely foggy' is NOT assumed — 'may' shows uncertainty about whether fog will occur.

questions.stem: Statement: 'Vote for Candidate X — a leader who will change the future.' Which assumption is implicit?

options.option_text: The future needs to be changed (correct: by saying Candidate X 'will change the future', the statement assumes the current state of the future needs changing ✓)
Candidate X will definitely win the election (not assumed — this is a campaign appeal, not a prediction)
Voters will change their minds based on slogans (this is about campaign effectiveness, not a direct assumption of this statement)
All other candidates are corrupt (the statement doesn't compare with others)

questions.explanation: A is correct. The phrase 'change the future' assumes that change in the future is desirable or necessary — i.e., the status quo or future trajectory needs changing. This is the implicit value judgment behind the campaign appeal. The other options either go beyond what's stated or add information not in the statement.
